generation_method: Manually assessed against executable evidence gathered during AFENDA Phase 2 (control plane). Unlike doctrine-registry.json / stack-registry.json / position-registry.json / authority-index.json, this file is not a pure deterministic text-extraction projection: implementation state is a judgment call that requires running real checks, not parsing prose. Structural completeness (every SCC-01..27 and V01..18 present exactly once, states drawn from the fixed enum) is itself verified by scripts/gate.mjs's control-map-completeness step.
policy: A control is never 'implemented' merely because a document describes it; implementation requires an executable check.
A critical executable control requires at least one red fixture proving the gate actually fails on a real injected violation.
Absence of application/database/frontend code is represented honestly as not-yet-built, not as a passing or skipped control.
'partial' means a real, currently-passing executable check exists but does not yet cover the full required scope; the gap is named in notes.

stack_controls.name: TypeScript native/compat parity
stack_controls.gate: pnpm run typecheck:native && pnpm run typecheck:compat && pnpm run lint
evidence: tsconfig.base.json (strict compiler options)
tsconfig.json (include scope)
package.json scripts typecheck:native / typecheck:native:single / typecheck:compat
eslint.config.mjs (type-aware lint via typescript-eslint)
stack_controls.notes: TypeScript 7 native (tsc, package @typescript/native@7.0.2) and TypeScript 6 compatibility (tsc6, package @typescript/typescript6@6.0.2) both install and run cleanly against the Phase 2 tooling surface (scripts/verify-toolchain-baseline.mjs, scripts/gate.mjs, scripts/red.mjs, scripts/generate-agent-docs.mjs). Phase 1 authority scripts (scripts/build-authority-registry.mjs, scripts/check-authority-integrity.mjs, scripts/lib/authority-parser.mjs) are deliberately excluded from tsconfig.json's include list: a real strict/checkJs run against them currently produces ~180 genuine implicit-any / unchecked-index errors (they predate this governance-language requirement and are load-bearing, already proven by their own self-tests). Retrofitting JSDoc types there is a real, separate task, not done in this phase to avoid destabilizing proven logic. Type-aware lint currently has no dedicated red fixture proving a real type error is caught (only a banned-comment fixture exists); typecheck itself has no injected-violation red fixture yet.
stack_controls.revisit_trigger: When the Phase 1 scripts are retrofitted with JSDoc types (or rewritten as .ts) and added to tsconfig.json's include list, and a red fixture exists proving typecheck:native/typecheck:compat actually fail on an injected type error.

pnpm-lock.yaml + .node-version + package.json engines/packageManager give a real dependency/toolchain lock (contributes to GOV-05's 'complete verification bundle' requirement, which did not exist before Phase 2)
red_fixtures: check-authority-integrity.mjs --self-test registry-drift-sensitive fixtures (alter rule_verbatim, omit V08, etc. all cause byte-identity/completeness to fail)
doctrine_verification_controls.notes: Proven only for the governance-registry generation layer (doctrine/stack/position -> governance/*.json) and the toolchain pin layer. NOT proven for the application/financial system: there is no migration, ledger, or generator determinism to test yet, and GOV-05's 'complete verification bundle' is not yet fully assembled (no CI execution observed from this environment, no application dependency graph). Marking this V-control implemented for the whole doctrine would overstate reality; 'partial' is the honest state.
doctrine_verification_controls.revisit_trigger: When application-layer generators (codegen, migrations) exist and can be shown to regenerate byte-identically with a red fixture for hidden toolchain change at that layer too.
